# API and Integration Security (API)

Rules for every HTTP API we build or call, including SAP RFC/BAPI integration and third-party services.

## SCS-API-01 Authenticate and authorize every API request by default

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Every API endpoint MUST require an authenticated caller and an authorization check before it processes the request. Anonymous endpoints are allowed only as explicit, commented exceptions (for example a health probe or the login endpoint).

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Set a fallback policy so endpoints without [Authorize] are still protected: AddAuthorizationBuilder().SetFallbackPolicy(new AuthorizationPolicyBuilder().RequireAuthenticatedUser().Build()).
- Apply [Authorize] to controllers (or RequireAuthorization() on route groups). Use [AllowAnonymous] only with a comment explaining why.
- [AllowAnonymous] on a class overrides [Authorize] on its actions; never put it at class level.
- Middleware that answers before UseAuthorization (Swagger, static files, health checks) is not protected by the fallback policy; secure it separately.

Verification: Endpoint inventory test: call every route without a token and expect 401, except the documented anonymous list.

## SCS-API-02 Use request and response DTOs; never bind or return entities

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: APIs MUST accept purpose-built request DTOs that contain only the fields the caller may set, and MUST return response DTOs that contain only the fields the caller may see. Database entities MUST NOT be bound from requests or returned in responses.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Never use [FromBody] SomeEntity, context.Update(entityFromRequest), SetValues(request) or a blind mapper.Map(request, entity).
- Project queries straight to DTOs with Select(...) so unneeded columns are never loaded.
- Use separate DTOs per role if different roles may see different fields.
- [Bind] / [BindNever] are ignored by the JSON input formatter, so only DTOs protect JSON APIs.

Verification: Code review greps for [FromBody] with entity types, SetValues( and return Ok(entity).

## SCS-API-03 Rate-limit and bound the resources every endpoint can consume

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: All APIs MUST apply rate limiting and throttling, and every endpoint MUST have explicit limits on request size, page size, upload size, execution time and outbound calls. This applies to internal APIs as well as external ones.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use the ASP.NET Core rate limiter: AddRateLimiter with RejectionStatusCode = 429 (the default is 503).
- Partition limits by authenticated user (sub claim), not by Host or X-Forwarded-For headers that clients can change.
- Apply stricter policies to login, OTP, password reset, token refresh, uploads, exports and any paid or SAP-heavy call.
- Cap page size on the server (never trust a client "take" value), set [RequestSizeLimit] per endpoint, and set timeouts on every outbound HttpClient call.
- Limiters are in memory per instance; if the API runs on several instances, use a shared store or a gateway limit.

Verification: Load test confirms 429 responses after the limit. Code review checks RequireRateLimiting on sensitive endpoints.

## SCS-API-04 Restrict CORS to an explicit allow-list of origins

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: CORS MUST be enabled only for an explicit list of exact origins. AllowAnyOrigin, wildcard origins, and reflecting any origin with credentials MUST NOT be used in production.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- AddCors(o => o.AddPolicy("web", p => p.WithOrigins("https://app.example.com").WithMethods(...).WithHeaders(...))). Use exact origins with no trailing slash.
- Never use AllowAnyOrigin(), WithOrigins("*"), or SetIsOriginAllowed(_ => true) with AllowCredentials().
- Native mobile apps do not need CORS. CORS is not access control; the API must still authenticate every request.
- Best option: serve the web front end from the same origin as the API so no CORS is needed.

Verification: Send a request with Origin: https://evil.example and confirm no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is returned.

## SCS-API-05 Version APIs and keep an inventory of all endpoints

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: APIs MUST be versioned so that changes are backward compatible and old versions can be deprecated in a controlled way. Each application MUST keep an up-to-date inventory of its API endpoints, versions and environments. Retired versions MUST be removed, not left running.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use Asp.Versioning.Http / Asp.Versioning.Mvc with URL segment versioning (/api/v1/...) as the standard pattern.
- Generate the OpenAPI document per version and keep it in the repository as the endpoint inventory.
- Expose OpenAPI / Swagger UI / Scalar only in Development, or behind RequireAuthorization(). .NET 9+ MapOpenApi has no authorization by default.
- Record deprecation dates in the change management task and remove old versions after the date.

Verification: Release checklist confirms the OpenAPI inventory is current and that no unlisted or deprecated routes respond in production.

Current gap: IT-56 ASR-20 records API versioning as partially implemented: used for major APIs, to be standardized across all services.

## SCS-API-06 Use least-privilege service accounts for SAP RFC/BAPI integration

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: SAP integration points (RFC/BAPI) MUST use dedicated service accounts per application with only the SAP authorization objects that application needs. Dialog or personal accounts MUST NOT be used for integration. SAP credentials MUST be kept in secure configuration (see SCS-SEC-02).

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- One SAP communication/system user per integration, with authorization objects limited to the function modules it calls (S_RFC restricted by function group / function name).
- Call function modules with typed parameters through the SAP .NET Connector (NCo); validate every value before sending.
- Treat SAP responses as untrusted input: validate types, lengths and ranges before storing or showing them.
- Use SNC (Secure Network Communications) or TLS for RFC traffic where the landscape supports it.
- Map application roles to SAP authorization objects where applicable, and review them with the SAP Basis team at least yearly.

Verification: Yearly review of SAP service user authorizations. Code review confirms parameterized NCo calls and secrets from Key Vault.

## SCS-API-07 Treat responses from third-party and internal services as untrusted

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Data received from other APIs, SAP, vendors, AI/LLM services or webhooks MUST be validated before it is stored, shown or used to make decisions. Calls to other services MUST use TLS, timeouts and limited retries.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Deserialize strictly into DTOs, reject unknown fields, and validate ranges and formats with Validator.ValidateObject(..., validateAllProperties: true).
- Use IHttpClientFactory / typed clients with a fixed BaseAddress; send API keys in headers, never in the URL.
- AddStandardResilienceHandler retries POST requests by default; cap retries (o.Retry.MaxRetryAttempts) or use idempotency keys for non-idempotent calls.
- Never build SQL, file paths, URLs or HTML from AI/LLM output. Send AI providers only the data the task needs.

Verification: Code review confirms typed validation of external responses. Tests feed malformed upstream responses and expect safe failure.

## SCS-API-08 Prevent server-side request forgery (SSRF)

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: The server MUST NOT fetch a URL taken from user input unless the scheme and host are on an allow-list. Outbound calls MUST go to fixed, configured hosts wherever possible, and MUST NOT be able to reach internal networks or cloud metadata addresses.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Configure typed HttpClients with a fixed BaseAddress and use relative paths.
- If a URL must come from input: allow-list scheme and host, resolve the name, and reject private, loopback and link-local ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, 169.254/16 including 169.254.169.254, and IPv6 equivalents).
- Set AllowAutoRedirect = false (the default keeps custom headers, including API keys, across redirects) and re-check the IP at connect time in SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback.
- Never return the raw upstream response to the caller.

Verification: Tests try internal IPs, localhost, metadata addresses and redirects, and expect rejection.
